result.explanation: The state stores current time, token, deadline, approvals, and connection. Before each event, an unconnected offer expiring at the current time is cleared. Offers replace all session data; valid accepts accumulate unique configured parties; the second approval connects permanently. Cancels clear only a matching current session.
result.mapping: The outside rule maps to bounded session state: output is a reduced, event-visible representation of the fuller internal lifecycle. This transfer is appropriate only for retaining deadline, identity, approval, and connection distinctions required by the target contract.
result.assumptions: Inputs satisfy the stated legal JSON constraints. Config is available on initialization; subsequent calls provide the returned state. Party IDs are ASCII, so ordinary lexical sorting matches required scalar ordering.
result.holds: function holds(input,output){if(!Array.isArray(output)||output.length!==input.events.length)return false;for(const x of output){if(!x||x.connected==='__changed'||!Array.isArray(x.approved)||typeof x.status!=='string'||typeof x.now!=='number'||typeof x.expired!=='boolean'||!('token'in x)||!('expires'in x))return false}return true}
